description: Ω5/W1 pack #2 — the import ontology as DECLARATIONS (GAP-M5 second pack: the W0 SCHEMA+CONTRACT+POLICY+TEST checklist, clean pass). Declares the shape of HARVESTED import data (T-05): where a recorded export came from (import.source), what an imported conversation is (import.conversation), what an imported message is (import.message), and the one boundary a parser family realizes (history.import@1, READ — a parser produces rows only; what is WRITTEN to ns chat is the writer's decision, W3). Passive v1: no ops, no capabilities, no dependencies. The implementing writer (a W3 chat-side harvest) carries the capabilities; this manifest only declares the domain. Retro-pass debt on pack #1 (domain-email) is filed beside it (packs/domain-email/DEBT.md).

fields.name: id
fields.doc: source identity: chatgpt | claude | gemini (the harvested parsers' provider identities; an unknown source REFUSES — fail-closed genealogy)

fields.name: mine
fields.doc: the pinned mine the export shape was grounded on, <repo>@<sha> (W0-9a; e.g. vivim-final-program@4a5eb84)

fields.name: originPath
fields.doc: path in the pinned mine the algorithm/shape was harvested from

fields.name: recordedOnly
fields.doc: must be true — the fixture pipeline imports recorded sessions only, never live network (W1 non-goal)

schema.doc: import.Source@1 — provenance of an import source: which mine, which path, recorded-only.

fields.name: externalId
fields.doc: source-native conversation id (legacy externalId grammar preserved per source)

fields.name: title
fields.doc: conversation title as recorded in the export (may be empty)

fields.name: createdAt
fields.doc: epoch ms from the export; 0 when the export carried no usable timestamp

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.doc: epoch ms from the export; 0 when absent

fields.name: messageCount
fields.doc: number of import.message rows following this conversation row in the parse

schema.doc: import.Conversation@1 — one parsed conversation (the parser's import.conversation row, persisted verbatim by a writer).

fields.name: externalId
fields.doc: source-native message id (legacy grammar preserved: mapping id for chatgpt, uuid_index for claude/gemini)

fields.name: role
fields.doc: user | assistant | system (legacy sender/author mapping preserved; unknown → user)

fields.name: content
fields.doc: message text (chatgpt string parts joined with newline; claude text/content-block extraction; gemini content)

fields.name: model
fields.doc: source-native model slug when the export carries one (chatgpt only)

fields.name: ts
fields.doc: epoch ms from the export; 0 when the export carried no usable timestamp — a parser never calls the clock (D-354 isolation, the one reviewed divergence from the legacy Date.now() fallback)

fields.name: tsEstimated
fields.doc: true when ts was absent/unusable in the export (ts=0) — attributable and byte-stable

schema.doc: import.Message@1 — one parsed message (the parser's import.message row, persisted verbatim by a writer).

contract.doc: import {source, exportText} → ordered ParsedChunk rows (import.conversation / import.message*n / import.done-final) through the version-pinned parser for the source (D-355 governance; the transform is pure, the transport off, recorded exports only). READ risk: the parse is vault-internal and writes nothing — the WRITER (W3 harvest) decides what lands in ns chat, carrying its own MUTATION bars. This contract names the boundary; v1 ships the parser family, the routable op lands with its writer.

policy.description: Domain policy for pack.domain-import: consent defaults and retention for imported conversation data — declarative data a law provider may consume (the parser itself is NOT routable and never gated; this policy binds the WRITER that materializes parsed rows).

consent.rationale: parsing recorded exports is vault-internal and writes nothing (READ); consent attaches to the WRITER's materialization ops (chat.* MUTATION rows), not to the parse.

retention.notes: imported rows persist as vault revisions (append-only Merkle chain); compaction may move superseded revisions cold but never deletes them; per-conversation retention follows the ns chat row (CHAT_HISTORY_CAP bounds reads, D-378).

transitions.doc: a W3 writer materializes a parsed message into ns chat as a conv/msg row citing the parser provenance (realizationRef + parserPins); v1 ships the parse, the transition lands with the writer

policy.doc: import.policy@1 — the import domain policy as data.

test.doc: pack conformance: ontology validation (schema field sets complete, contract risk class READ, namespace-clean ids, parsed→materialized state machine acyclic), plus the parser-family falsifiers living with the parser code (plugins/vivim-chat).

capabilities.justification: A pack is passive declarations: no ops to route, no ports to call, no host capabilities. The parser family (plugins/vivim-chat, D-355 parser contributions) registers no routable op; the implementing writer (W3) carries the capabilities when it lands.
